ai-llude: Ask for AI text at your caret in one of two forms: a smooth continuation, or four rough unrelated fragments meant to be rewritten.
alt-takes: Mark a stretch of text as having alternatives.
anti-hemmingway: Greys out every word except adjectives and adverbs, so your modifiers stand out against a faded page.
bubbles-view: Shows your document as small bubbles drifting around a field, one per paragraph, instead of a page.
card-links: Shows your document as a canvas of cards, one per block, that you can edit and drag wherever you like.
cards-view: Turns a pane into a corkboard with one editable card per paragraph, heading or list.

deictic-highlighter: Colours words that point to the speaker, place or moment of a text, in five groups: personal words like I and you, places like here, times like now, connectives like however, and forms of address like sir.
deleted-words-printer: Counts each whole word you delete, and after every few cut words prints a small sticker listing them on a Bluetooth thermal printer at your desk.
disappearing-sentences: As you write, sentences you have moved past fade to a faint grey a second after your caret leaves them, so only what you are working on stays clear.
document-viewer: Makes a pane read-only so you can look at a document without changing it by accident.
giblets-file: Words and passages you delete are quietly added to a second document you choose, shown in a column beside your editor.
glas-columns: Shows two columns: your text on the left and private notes on the right, each level with the paragraph it comments on.
graveyard: Words you delete are collected in a graveyard section at the end of the same document, one entry per cut, so your cuttings travel with the file.
haiku-sampler: Finds a 5-7-5 haiku made only of your own words, in the order you wrote them, and shows it in a small card.
heavy-words: A random word in your first paragraph turns red and slowly sinks down the page, one line at a time, wedging itself between other words.
hemingway-pen: Switch on a pen, then drag the mouse over your text like a paintbrush.
highlight-search: Highlight passages in yellow as you read or write, then search only inside what you highlighted.
karaoke-reader: Press Read and your whole document is spoken aloud in your device's voice, with each word highlighted as it is said, so your eye keeps its place.
margin-notes: Select some text and add a note, and it appears in the page margin beside that line, like pencilled marginalia.

poet-critique: Highlight some lines and ask for a critique, and a small pixel-art cartoon of a famous poet answers in a panel beside your text, with a speech bubble giving feedback in that poet's voice.
prosody: For poets writing in a set form.
read-aloud: Place the caret, press Cmd-Shift-S (Ctrl-Shift-S elsewhere), and the document is read aloud from there to the end in your device's voice.
resizable-split: Splits the page into two or more areas, side by side or stacked, for example two drafts, or an outline above your text.
revision-stash: When you can't choose between phrasings, write them one after another, select them, and pick which one stays.
sentence-cycler: Hover over a paragraph with two or more sentences and each sentence is tinted in a different colour.
sentence-flipper: Shows every sentence turned around: statements become questions, and questions become statements.
sentence-length: Tints every sentence by its word count on one scale, from red for the shortest to magenta for the longest, so the rhythm of your prose shows at a glance.
sentence-length-spectrum: Tints each sentence by how far its length is from your document's typical length.
sentence-spacing: Click into a paragraph, or select across a few, and its sentences spread apart with wide gaps so you can look at them one at a time.
speech-to-text: Press the microphone button and speak.

topic-sentence-highlighting: Highlights the first sentence of every paragraph and blurs the rest, so your document reads as a skeleton of topic sentences and you can check whether each paragraph states its point up front.
two-tone: Text is either green, for draft, or pink, for keepers.
unfamiliar-words: Marks every word that is not on a list of familiar, everyday words, so jargon and complicated vocabulary stand out.

word-processor: The everyday formatting kit: bold, italic, underline, bullet and numbered lists, headings, indent, font size and family, and text colour, from a toolbar and the usual keyboard shortcuts.
writor: A writing-center tutor for a draft you are revising.
